rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate shifts the table toward stronger obfuscation while protecting the hot path: almabench is a small (4417 text bytes, 5 functions) numeric benchmark whose bulk sits in the planetpv loop, so cheap, low-risk transformations are pushed hard — SUB (arithmetic substitution), SPLIT (basic-block splitting), and the data/pointer-disguising ICALL and IGV get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with generous cost tolerances, since they add real reverse-engineering friction at negligible runtime price across all five functions. The expensive control-flow transforms are deliberately restrained: BCF and IBR get strong security weights but tight RuntimeCost (0.35/0.40) so the selector applies them only where loop structure permits (e.g., the cold main/radecdist/anpm bodies rather than planetpv's inner loop), and FLA is held at RuntimeCost 0.30 with moderate security weight to avoid flattening the tight numeric kernels where it would both tank performance and yield little since those loops are already opaque after SUB+SPLIT. CorrectnessRisk weights on the three restructuring passes (BCF 0.8, FLA 0.7, IBR 0.75) stay permissive enough to keep coverage given the clean round-0 build, while the trivially safe passes keep 0.85-0.9, preserving the validated correctness margin as overall obfuscation pressure rises.
